name: All Hands and Hearts: schools and relief abroad (charityevals' estimate)
beneficiaries_note: Our build: the Myanmar earthquake response and school rebuilds in Nepal, the Philippines and Mexico: shares of the result at the defaults.
summary: All Hands and Hearts' work abroad in the year to August 2025 (the latest audited year; its Afghanistan and Gaza responses began after it): the Myanmar earthquake response through local partners (cash, water, shelter materials and hygiene supplies, then a water and hygiene programme in 12 villages: 13,000 people), and school rebuilds for disaster-hit communities (Bandevi School in Nepal, two bamboo-frame schools in the Philippines and 17 classrooms repaired in Oaxaca, Mexico). Its accounts don't split spending by country, so the $2.0 million modelled here is our judgment of the share abroad (18%, from 10% to 30%), which moves the result in proportion. The relief is valued as goods at their cost on the site's log-income scale at the affected households' consumption, plus the few excess deaths clean water and shelter avert; each school as its building's cost spread over its pupils and years, for the years it brought forward. The result, about 0.09 years of healthy life per $1,000 (0.015 to 0.5), is near the median global-health charity and about the American Red Cross's relief abroad; three-quarters of it is the Myanmar relief, valued at a judged $40 a person. Both branches are discounted for missing data: the counts are All Hands and Hearts' own and what each person got is a judgment. The biggest uncertainties are the share of spending abroad, the value of the relief per person and what others would have done anyway.

sections.explainer: Discounts for weaker evidence, what would have happened anyway, credit shared with others, and delivery falling short. All multiply the outcome.

sections.title: Other outcomes, in this model's unit
sections.explainer: charityevals' standard step for outcomes in more than one unit (docs/normalization.md 2.6): each outcome is counted in its own unit (units of value for income and deaths, WELLBYs for life satisfaction, tonnes of CO₂e, chicken pain days) and put into this model's unit by its unit's conversion over this unit's, which the headline's conversion cancels. So each moves only with its own sliders, exactly as in a model of its own unit. The rows are fixed; don't edit them.

rows.label: People reached by the Myanmar earthquake response

source.title: All Hands and Hearts, Annual Report 2025: A Year in Review
source.quote: 13K+ people reached by All Hands & Hearts relief in the months since the earthquake

rows.explainer: Cash, clean water, shelter materials, clothing and hygiene supplies to 4,400 people in the first two weeks, then a water, sanitation and hygiene programme (boreholes rebuilt, water filters, hygiene education, psychosocial support) in 12 villages reaching more than 9,000, all through local partners from Thailand. The low end is the WASH programme's 9,000 alone, in case the totals overlap or the 13,000 (counted in a report of November 2025) includes people reached after 31 August.

rows.label: People reached
rows.explainer: Students in the schools and people reached by the relief.

rows.label: Cost per person reached
rows.explainer: Context: the full cash cost over everyone reached.

rows.label: Cost of rebuilding a school, Nepal
rows.explainer: Our judgment, anchored on All Hands and Hearts' Nepal flood campaign (programme start August 2026): 'raise $5 million to rebuild 20 schools' (allhandsandhearts.org/our-work/programs/nepal-flood-relief, retrieved 2026-11-14), $250,000 a school by our division, a forward goal rather than a stated cost per school. What the building is worth at its cost: $250,000, from $150,000 (a smaller school, cheaper in 2024-25) to $350,000.

rows.label: Cost of rebuilding a school, Philippines
rows.explainer: Our judgment: bamboo-frame schools of a few classrooms built with local labour and volunteers cost less than Nepal's masonry schools; half the Nepal figure, from a quarter to the same.

rows.label: Cost of repairing a classroom, Mexico
rows.explainer: Our judgment: repairing a storm-damaged classroom's roof, ceiling and walls (not rebuilding it) costs a few thousand to $20,000 in Mexico. $8,000.

rows.label: Years a rebuilt school serves
rows.explainer: Our judgment: a disaster-resilient masonry or cement-bamboo school lasts decades; maintenance and later disasters cut that. 30, from 15 to 50.

rows.label: Years a classroom repair lasts
rows.explainer: Our judgment: a repaired roof and ceiling last a decade or so. 10, from 5 to 20.

rows.label: Value of a school to its users, as a share of its cost
rows.explainer: Our judgment: what families would give up for the school's use as a share of what it cost to build. A safe classroom in place of a temporary shelter is worth a lot to them, but a building is a lumpy, public good they would not buy at its full price, and part of its cost is the resilient design whose value (lives in a future earthquake or typhoon) is in unmodelled benefits. Below the 0.8 of US housing in kind. 0.6, from 0.3 to 0.9.

rows.label: Pupils' households' consumption against their country's survey mean
rows.explainer: Our judgment: rural public schools serve households poorer than the national mean (Nepal's bottom 40% consume about half the mean). As Habitat for Humanity's model for Asia and the Pacific (0.65): 0.7, from 0.45 to 1.

rows.label: Consumption per person, Nepal (2024 US$)
rows.explainer: Nepal's survey mean (2022, 2021 PPP dollars) a year, in 2024 US prices, carried to 2024 by 0.7 of growth per person, at Nepal's 2024 price level: nominal 2024 dollars, the units of the school's cost.

rows.label: Income per person, Philippines (2024 US$)
rows.explainer: As for Nepal; the Philippines' survey measures income (full growth passed through).

rows.label: Income per person, Mexico (2024 US$)
rows.explainer: As for Nepal; Mexico's survey (2024) measures income.

rows.label: Nepal school: log-consumption gain per pupil over the school's life
rows.formula: sch_inkind_value * ln(1 + sch_cost_npl / sch_students_per_school / pv_annuity_due(1, $discount_rate, sch_years_new) / (cons_npl * sch_targeting)) * pv_annuity_due(1, $discount_rate, sch_years_new)
rows.explainer: The school's cost as an even yearly flow over its life (its present value equals the cost at the shared discount rate), per pupil, on the log scale at the pupils' households' consumption per person, over those years: each year's pupils get that year's share.

rows.label: Philippines school: log-consumption gain per pupil over the school's life
rows.formula: sch_inkind_value * ln(1 + sch_cost_phl / sch_students_per_school / pv_annuity_due(1, $discount_rate, sch_years_new) / (cons_phl * sch_targeting)) * pv_annuity_due(1, $discount_rate, sch_years_new)
rows.explainer: As for Nepal.

rows.label: Mexico repairs: log-consumption gain per pupil over the repairs' life
rows.formula: sch_inkind_value * ln(1 + sch_classrooms_mex * sch_cost_per_classroom_mex / sch_students_mex / pv_annuity_due(1, $discount_rate, sch_years_repair) / (cons_mex * sch_targeting)) * pv_annuity_due(1, $discount_rate, sch_years_repair)
rows.explainer: As for Nepal, over the repairs' years.

rows.label: Schools: units of value before adjustments
rows.explainer: Schools: units of value before adjustments

rows.label: Death rate of the people reached in the months after the earthquake
rows.explainer: Our judgment: the 28 March 2025 earthquake killed thousands at once (not averted by relief that came after); in the months after, deaths among the displaced and those without water rise somewhat above normal from diarrhoea, exposure and lost care, in a country already in conflict. 11 per 1,000 a year, from 8 to 20.

rows.label: Normal death rate in Myanmar
rows.explainer: Our judgment, anchored on Myanmar's crude death rate of about 8 per 1,000 a year (UN World Population Prospects). 8, from 7 to 9.5.

rows.label: Share of the excess deaths the relief averted
rows.explainer: Our judgment: clean water, filters and hygiene supplies cut diarrhoeal disease after disasters, and shelter materials exposure, but cash and kits do little against most excess deaths. The research: the Cochrane review of water and sanitation in emergencies finds lower diarrhoea with water treatment, without mortality data (Yates et al. 2017 is narrative); the American Red Cross's international model takes 3% for cash and relief items. With more water work here, 4%, from 0 to 12%.

rows.label: Years of the crisis the relief covers
rows.explainer: Our judgment: emergency relief in the first two weeks, then a water and hygiene programme over the following months: about four months, from one to six.

rows.label: Deaths averted per person reached
rows.explainer: Excess deaths over the months covered, times the share the response averts.

rows.label: Share of excess deaths averted under five
rows.explainer: Our judgment: after a sudden-onset disaster in a middle-income country, excess deaths from water-borne disease, exposure and lost care fall most on young children and the old, fewer of them under five than in famines (often 40-60%). Myanmar's under-five share of all deaths is lower still, since its population is ageing. 25%, from 15% to 40%.

rows.label: Share aged 5-14 of excess deaths over five
rows.explainer: Our judgment: older children have the lowest death rates of any age; about 8% of deaths over five, up to 18% if diarrhoeal outbreaks strike children more.

rows.label: Share aged 15-49 of excess deaths over fifteen
rows.explainer: Our judgment: working-age adults die less than the old after disasters but are a large share of the population; 30%, from 20% to 45%. The rest are valued at the site's 50-74 band.

rows.label: Value of a death averted
rows.explainer: The site's one value of a death, by age band, times your value of a life.

rows.label: Illness averted per person, healthy years
rows.explainer: 0: the diarrhoea averted by the water work has no measured effect here; it is in unmodelled benefits beside the deaths, and the psychosocial support too.

rows.label: Relief delivered per person, Myanmar
rows.explainer: Our judgment of the cash, water, shelter materials, clothing, hygiene supplies, filters and repaired boreholes per person reached, in 2025 US dollars: a few dollars of hygiene items for some, $20-50 of cash or shelter materials for others, and boreholes and filters shared by villages. $40, from $15 to $100, below the American Red Cross's $70 for appeals with large cash transfers.

rows.label: PPP factor, Myanmar
rows.explainer: The template's canonical row, kept for reading and comparison only: the relief and the baseline below are both in nominal US dollars, so the price level cancels in the log gain and no row reads it.

rows.label: Household consumption as a share of GDP, Myanmar
rows.explainer: Our judgment, as in the American Red Cross's international model: the World Bank has no consumption series for Myanmar; neighbouring Bangladesh's households consume 70% of GDP (NE.CON.PRVT.ZS, 2024). 0.7, from 0.55 to 0.8.

rows.label: Affected households' consumption against Myanmar's survey mean
rows.explainer: Our judgment: the villages near Mandalay and Sagaing reached by the water programme are rural and hit by the earthquake, so poorer than the national mean, but the earthquake struck a broad population, not the poorest only. 0.8, from 0.55 to 1.05.

rows.label: Affected households' consumption per person a year, Myanmar
rows.explainer: Myanmar's GDP per person (World Bank, 2024 US$) times households' share of it, put on the household-survey scale by the site's shared ratio for a country with no recent survey (@survey_consumption.survey_to_na_world_median, 0.68), at the affected households' share: about $520 a year.

rows.label: Relief: log-consumption gain per person
rows.explainer: The relief's value on the site's one log-income scale at the affected households' consumption, counted once.

rows.label: Relief: units of value before adjustments
rows.explainer: Relief: units of value before adjustments

rows.label: Schools: evidence
rows.explainer: Our judgment, validity only: schools and classrooms are counted and the value is the building at its cost (no effect study needed); the pupils per school and the cost per school are rows of their own. 0.85, from 0.6 to 1.

rows.label: Schools: share that wouldn't have happened anyway
rows.explainer: Our judgment, years brought forward and the counterfactual as one question: Nepal's pupils were in temporary structures a decade after the 2015 earthquakes, so its school would have waited long; in the Philippines and Mexico the education departments and other groups rebuild sooner, and some repairs would have come within a year or two. 0.5, from 0.25 to 0.8.

rows.label: Schools: All Hands and Hearts' share of the resources
rows.explainer: Our judgment: communities give labour (parents volunteered on the Philippines schools), local governments land and some materials, and international volunteers their time (All Hands and Hearts houses and feeds them, in its cost). Donated materials and equipment ($1,060,843, partly for the schools) are taken out of the cost, so they belong here too. Less shared than the US work (0.52 there, where volunteers' hours are about half the resources), since the schools are built mostly by paid local masons and contractors in All Hands and Hearts' cost. 0.7, from 0.45 to 0.9.

rows.label: Schools: work counted that wasn't finished
rows.explainer: Our judgment: the schools are counted as completed, but some may be used below capacity or need further work. 0.95, from 0.85 to 1.

rows.label: Relief: evidence
rows.explainer: Our judgment: the relief's value is its goods and cash at their cost (no effect study needed), and the people reached are All Hands and Hearts' rounded count. The American Red Cross's relief model takes 0.95. 0.9, from 0.7 to 1.

rows.label: Relief: share that wouldn't have happened anyway
rows.explainer: Our judgment: Myanmar's earthquake response was badly underfunded in a country at war, where many agencies could not reach villages, so less of the relief would have come from others; some villages got help from other local groups. 0.6, from 0.35 to 0.85.

rows.label: Relief: All Hands and Hearts' share of the resources
rows.explainer: Our judgment: the relief went out through local partners, whose staff, volunteers and other funding are resources behind it beside All Hands and Hearts' money. 0.7, from 0.4 to 0.9.

rows.label: Relief: delivered as counted
rows.explainer: Our judgment: goods lost, diverted or misdirected in a conflict setting. 0.9, from 0.75 to 1.

rows.label: Leverage and funging
rows.explainer: Our judgment: other funders' fill-in is in the counterfactuals; no government pays for this work in All Hands and Hearts' place. 1, from 0.9 to 1.05.

rows.label: Schools: missing-data step
rows.explainer: Thin: the schools and classrooms are counted, but the pupils in two of them, the cost of the Philippines and Mexico work and the value to the pupils are judgments.

rows.label: Relief: missing-data step
rows.explainer: Thin: the people reached are counted, but what each got and the deaths averted are judgments from research on relief in other crises.

rows.label: Schools: all adjustments
rows.formula: sch_evidence_adj * sch_counterfactual_adj * sch_attribution_share * sch_implementation_adj * leverage_funging_adj * sch_missing_data_adj
rows.explainer: Schools: all adjustments

rows.label: Relief: all adjustments
rows.formula: rel_evidence_adj * rel_counterfactual_adj * rel_attribution_share * rel_implementation_adj * leverage_funging_adj * rel_missing_data_adj
rows.explainer: Relief: all adjustments

rows.label: Benefits and harms not modelled, as a share of modelled value
rows.explainer: Our judgment, each effect with its sign: children back in school sooner and learning in a safe, dry classroom, with later earnings (+; the school's cost already stands for part of its worth to families, so a share); pupils' lives saved in a future earthquake or typhoon by the resilient design (+); the Female Mason Training Program's livelihoods for women in Nepal (+); diarrhoea averted and psychosocial support in Myanmar (+); international volunteers' own wellbeing (+, small); local builders displaced (-, small). +20%, from -5% to +50%.

rows.label: Units of value, adjusted
rows.explainer: Each branch's units of value times its own adjustments (Convention 4): the schools' log gains and the relief's goods and deaths averted.

rows.label: Healthy years from units of value
rows.explainer: The bridge from UoV into healthy years (docs/normalization.md 2.6): fixed, don't edit.

rows.explainer: The bridge from WELLBYs into healthy years (docs/normalization.md 2.6): fixed, don't edit.

rows.explainer: Every outcome in healthy years, each branch already adjusted (Convention 4), times the share for effects not modelled.
